checks: The proper endpoint cuts make a minimizing cap pass through the mark by threshold reduction, and root equality makes the middle captured volume positive. The accepted translation equality makes all three cut faces translates with equal positive section measure and midpoint centroid identity.

For a continuous normal velocity a with adjusted threshold a·y, the first variation is the common positive normalized coarea times a·(c_-+c_0+c_+-3y). Stationarity and c_0=(c_-+c_+)/2 give c_0=y. The volume-preserving shear sends c_+ and c_- to zero and removes the old integer coefficient with the stated sign.

A facet meeting s=0 must have a positive-height vertex because no vertex is on the cut and the facet is convex. Hence it contributes a facet plane of the common positive cap. All remaining old facets are strictly slack on the compact section, giving one common slab by compactness.

With no old vertex on the plane, fixed edge incidences and their smooth intersections yield a fixed triangulation and a C² volume. A small threshold or tilt only changes membership in the common slab. The exact endpoint thresholds are beta and -beta.

The mixed v,beta derivatives cancel, the three identical v blocks add, and both beta second derivatives add. These are through-mark caps, so the local minimum gives PSD. F_t=-sigma at unit normal gives the sign of sigma prime. Original §7 (8)–(10) matches.

dependencies.hypotheses: The original nonvertical cap at the fixed mark is depth attaining with proper endpoints, positive middle capture and exact captured-side root equality. The three captured bodies and their positive cutting faces are translates.

Use only the standalone full ambient first-variation formula in §2 on these three positive polytopal fibers. All cuts are proper by the preceding equality lemma, so the zero-section exception and the unrelated projected-contact hypotheses do not enter.

overlap.comparison: Gives congruent positive caps and proper sections but not the common two-sided germ or the Hessian test.
Its Hessian is for an integrated positive part and fixed-mass barycenter support, not the raw cap volume with varying angle and integer coefficient.

readability: The two-sided neighborhood refers to a neighborhood of the common section in the transformed coordinates.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The positive proper section measures and fixed-mark first variation center the common cut. The no-vertex hypothesis identifies its local geometry and gives the exact three-term cap formula with a positive-semidefinite Hessian.
